item.title: Personal Finance (4): Index Funds and ETFs — The Lazy Investor's Edge
item.description:
I spent years thinking investing meant picking stocks. Then I learned index funds, and the main thing I felt was annoyance — not at the idea, which is beautifully simple, but at myself for wasting so many evenings on stock-picking fantasies. You don’t have to beat the market. You can just be it.

What Is an Index?#

An index is a rules-based list of assets — usually stocks — each given a weight and rebalanced on a schedule. The CSI 300 tracks the 300 largest, most liquid A-shares. The S&P 500 does the same for 500 large-cap US firms. MSCI Emerging Markets spans ~1,400 companies across 24 economies.

item.title: Personal Finance (2): The Product Zoo — From Money Market Funds to Gold
item.description:
Part 1 was about why you spread money across baskets. This is about what the baskets are. Open a bank’s wealth app and the buttons — “Fixed income enhanced,” “Structured deposit,” “FOF,” “Quantitative neutral” — assume you already know what you’re shopping for. Here’s the field guide, one asset class at a time, plus the one table I wish someone had handed me on day one.

The Whole Zoo on One Page#

Everything below fits in a single map. Ranges are typical over a rate cycle; the bracketed figures are current levels as of mid-2026, when Chinese rates hit record lows. The point is the relative position of each animal, not a quotable yield.
